local_snapshot_notes: A point-in-time copy of every External-tab row (all 14 columns) is saved in external-tab-snapshot.json. Prefer this local snapshot for normal retrieval instead of re-fetching the live workbook; only re-fetch when the snapshot is stale (see staleness_check) or a question needs material newer than the snapshot's retrieved_at date.
access_notes: This workbook is IRM/RMS-protected (Azure Information Protection), not just link-gated. A plain HTTP fetch of the sharing URL returns 401, and downloading the raw bytes and parsing them with a local library (e.g. openpyxl) fails because the content is cryptographically sealed. The only way to read it is through a Microsoft 365 service that can honor the user's RMS license (e.g. Copilot/workiq acting under the signed-in user's identity). Resolve the sharing link to a direct item webUrl first if needed, then ask that service to read the 'External' worksheet in small batches (~10 rows at a time) to avoid truncation.
expected_columns: Priority to add to context library

staleness_check.on_expiry: Re-run the workiq-retrieve + workiq-ask extraction against workbook_url (External worksheet only), rewrite external-tab-snapshot.json with the new rows, and update observed_date/observed_range/observed_record_count here and in source-priority.md. Then re-derive catalog.json priority_tier/research_questions fields from the refreshed snapshot.
